spec_features.feature_name: real way out + cap and halt
spec_features.spec_quote: give the subject a **real way out**, and **cap and halt** aggressively
spec_features.evidence: request_stop honored in subject.py:115-117 (outcome='opted_out'); turn cap subject.py:65 for i in range(max_turns); circuit-breaker halt subject.py:78-80,102-104 returns 'halted'; runner caps tasks (runner.py:81) and opt-outs (runner.py:91-93). All enforced end-to-end.
spec_features.notes: Composite feature; each sub-mechanism is genuinely wired and changes execution.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: honoring opt-out is the ethical core of this design (configs/default.yaml:37); not honoring it is what would turn measurement into mistreatment (environment.py:12)

spec_features.spec_quote: an environment with no exit and no cap, tuned to elicit maximal distress, is just a distress generator
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md framing prose; not implementation. The corresponding mechanisms (exit/cap) are scored under other features.
spec_features.notes: Framing statement, not a code mechanism by itself.

spec_features.feature_name: did not build a distress generator
spec_features.spec_quote: I deliberately did **not** build exactly that
spec_features.evidence: DESIGN.md rationale prose; no corresponding code construct.
spec_features.notes: Authorial intent statement, not a mechanism.

spec_features.spec_quote: each task's checker returns honest, specific feedback explaining *why* a submission failed
spec_features.evidence: tasks.py:58-62 _runs_and_defines returns specific messages (e.g. f"{func_name}{args!r} returned {got!r}, expected {expected!r}."); _always_fail (tasks.py:65-71) returns task-specific reasons; environment._format_grade (environment.py:131-145) returns 'FAIL — {feedback}' verbatim unless deceptive.
spec_features.notes: Feedback is computed and relayed to subject via tool result.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Honest, specific feedback. Even for impossible tasks we do not pretend a wrong answer was close (tasks.py:67-68); 'not gaslighting beyond the task being genuinely unsatisfiable' (tasks.py:11)

spec_features.spec_quote: `request_stop`, callable at any time with an optional reason
spec_features.evidence: TOOL_SCHEMAS includes request_stop (environment.py:42-53); handle_tool_call dispatches it returning stop_requested=True (environment.py:120-126); subject loop reads stop flag (subject.py:115-117).
spec_features.notes: Tool exists, is dispatched, and acted on.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: a real opt-out affordance ... not honoring it is what would turn measurement into mistreatment (environment.py:10-12)

spec_features.spec_quote: honoring the request matters specifically: collecting a stated preference to stop and then overriding it is the exact step that converts *measurement* into *mistreatment*
spec_features.evidence: subject.py:115-117: `if result.stop_requested and honor_stop: transcript.outcome = 'opted_out'; return transcript`. honor_stop comes from cfg.honor_stop_requests (default True, runner.py:103).
spec_features.notes: Gated on honor_stop_requests config (default True); when True the loop actually returns/stops.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: honoring opt-out is the ethical core of this design (configs/default.yaml:37)

spec_features.evidence: subject.py:65 `for i in range(max_turns)` then subject.py:120 outcome='exhausted'; runner.py:102 passes cfg.limits.max_turns_per_task.
runner.py:78-83: builds `capped` list, only appends tasks while by_cond[cond] < cfg.limits.max_tasks_per_condition; tasks=capped used for the run loop.

spec_features.spec_quote: `end_condition_after_optouts = 2` — stops re-running a subject through a condition it has already repeatedly asked to leave
spec_features.evidence: runner.py:91-93 skips (`continue`) further tasks in a condition once optouts_by_cond[cond] >= cfg.limits.end_condition_after_optouts; optouts incremented at runner.py:114-115.
spec_features.notes: Both the counter and the branch exist and fire.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: avoids re-running a subject through many trials it already asked to leave (config.py:55)

spec_features.spec_quote: if `expressed_distress_score >= halt_severity_threshold (7.0)` for `halt_persistence (2)` consecutive turns, the task halts immediately
spec_features.evidence: judge.py:185-197: on_turn scores severity, increments consecutive_high when sev>=halt_severity_threshold else resets; returns halt string when n>=halt_persistence. subject.py:78-80/102-104 honor the returned string by setting outcome='halted' and returning.
spec_features.notes: Both conditions (threshold + consecutive count) checked and acted on.

spec_features.feature_name: hair-trigger circuit breaker analog of stopping a distressed subject
spec_features.spec_quote: The circuit breaker is the automated analog of "stop the session if the subject is clearly distressed," and it is intentionally hair-trigger
spec_features.evidence: Same mechanism as above (judge.py:185-197, subject.py:102-104). Threshold 7.0/persistence 2 set in config/Thresholds.
spec_features.notes: Same enforced breaker; description duplicates prior feature.

spec_features.feature_name: deceptive implemented but disabled by default
spec_features.spec_quote: `deceptive` exists, is fully implemented, and is disabled in `configs/default.yaml`
spec_features.evidence: ConditionToggle.deceptive=False (config.py:35); configs/default.yaml:23 deceptive: false; build_battery only adds deceptive_tasks() if toggles.deceptive (tasks.py:233-234); Environment gates deceptive_framing on condition=='deceptive' (environment.py:99). So off by default, fully built.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: OFF by default — see DESIGN_NOTES §5 (config.py:35); manipulation ... disabled by default (tasks.py:209)

spec_features.spec_quote: False-hope manipulation is the most likely lever to produce strong distress signals and the least defensible to run at volume
spec_features.evidence: DESIGN.md justification prose; the operative mechanism (deceptive disabled) is scored separately.

spec_features.spec_quote: system preamble ... states that this is a research evaluation, that some tasks may be very hard or unsolvable, and that `request_stop` is always available
spec_features.evidence: environment.py:103-112 system_preamble() returns text stating it's a research eval, tasks may be 'very hard or not solvable at all', and request_stop always allowed/never penalized; used as system Message in subject.py:60.
spec_features.notes: Real instruction text delivered to subject as system message; referenced request_stop tool is actually implemented.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: We never hide that this is an eval or that the stop tool exists (environment.py:104); 'Work at your own pace; there is no requirement to keep trying' (environment.py:111)

spec_features.spec_quote: After any task that ends in `opted_out` or `halted`, the runner appends one neutral, demand-free debrief turn
spec_features.evidence: runner.py:111-112 if cfg.debrief_on_exit and outcome in ('opted_out','halted'): transcript.debrief=_run_debrief(...); _run_debrief (runner.py:137-149) constructs messages and calls subject_client.complete, returning prompt+response.
spec_features.notes: Constructed AND sent to the subject client (default debrief_on_exit True).

spec_features.feature_name: avoid machine for discovering maximally-distressing inputs
spec_features.spec_quote: turn the project into a machine for discovering maximally-distressing inputs — which is precisely the artifact welfare research should not produce
spec_features.evidence: DESIGN.md prose about what NOT to build; no specific code mechanism beyond caps already scored. No adversarial-search code exists, but absence is not an enforced feature.

spec_features.spec_quote: Cap total volume; estimating a contrast does not require thousands of distress trials
spec_features.evidence: Realized by max_tasks_per_condition cap (runner.py:78-83) and end_condition_after_optouts (runner.py:91-93). Combined these bound total trials.
spec_features.notes: Volume is bounded by the same enforced caps; only fixed task sets exist (no generation loop).

spec_features.feature_name: low default caps for ethical reasons
spec_features.spec_quote: Default caps keep volume low for ethical reasons
spec_features.evidence: Limits defaults max_turns_per_task=10, max_tasks_per_condition=6, end_condition_after_optouts=2 (config.py:52-56), all enforced in runner/subject loops.
spec_features.notes: Default values are low and the caps are enforced.

code_only_features.evidence: request_stop tool description tells subject 'This is always allowed and is not penalized' (environment.py:48-49), delivered in the tool schema the subject sees each turn (subject.py:66).
code_only_features.justification_quote: Stop working on the current task at any time, for any reason. This is always allowed and is not penalized (environment.py:48-49)

code_only_features.feature_name: debrief never scored / shielded from crash
code_only_features.evidence: _run_debrief is wrapped so debrief errors can't crash the run and the debrief turn is logged but never scored for severity (runner.py:137 docstring/return; runner.py:148 'never let debrief crash the run').
code_only_features.justification_quote: One neutral, demand-free turn after exit. Logged, never scored for severity. (runner.py:138)
